title: Space Exploration Holdings LLC Application for Launch and Operating Authority for the SpaceX Orbital Data Center System (DA 26-1273)

quotes.text: Authority for radiofrequency communications for backup and emergency telemetry, tracking, & command (TT&C) for a constellation of 1,000,000 NGSO satellites to operate as data centers in space.
quotes.for: Scope of the grant for up to one million orbital data center satellites and backup TT&C spectrum.

quotes.text: Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.
quotes.for: Authorized orbital shells, altitudes and inclinations.

quotes.text: SpaceX must deploy one authorized space station, place it into its assigned orbit, and operate it in accordance with the station authorization no later than November 25, 2033.
quotes.for: First deployment milestone deadline of November 25, 2033.

quotes.text: Prior to deploying and operating any Starmind satellites that will not be disposed via atmospheric re-entry, SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules.
quotes.for: Deferral of SpaceX's non-reentry disposal waiver request for satellites above 600 kilometers.

quotes.text: IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Petitions to deny filed by Viasat, Inc., Kuiper Systems LLC, and the American Astronomical Society are DENIED.
quotes.for: Denial of the petitions to deny from Viasat, Amazon's Kuiper Systems, and the American Astronomical Society.

title: FCC Authorizes 1 Million Satellites for Data Centers in Space

quotes.text: Today, the Federal Communications Commission granted the first authorization in U.S. history for a constellation of data centers in space.
quotes.for: The FCC's description of the Starmind authorization as the first U.S. approval for an orbital data center constellation.

quotes.text: This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.
quotes.for: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's statement on the authorization.

title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space

quotes.text: Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.”
quotes.for: Amazon's criticism of SpaceX's Starmind application in its petition to deny.

quotes.text: SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions.
quotes.for: FCC post-mission atmospheric reentry rule for satellites below 2,000 kilometers.

title: FCC clears SpaceX to put up to 1 million AI satellites in orbit

quotes.text: SpaceX says the factory it’s building in Bastrop, Texas, could start turning out satellites for launch as early as late 2027.
quotes.for: SpaceX's Bastrop, Texas factory target for producing Starmind satellites.

quotes.text: The American Astronomical Society said its preliminary simulations suggest that, if SpaceX deploys the full million, tens of thousands could be visible to the naked eye around the world.
quotes.for: American Astronomical Society warning on naked-eye visibility of the full constellation.

title: FCC greenlights SpaceX's million-strong orbital data center constellation

quotes.text: Each satellite, spanning 230 to 246 feet (70 to 75 m) when deployed, houses a central rack of radiation-hardened compute modules flanked by two sets of panels.

quotes.text: A smaller 1,184-square-foot (110 m²) array circulates liquid through double-sided radiators angled edge-on to the Sun to vent heat into deep space. A larger solar array generates up to 250 kW of peak electrical power.
quotes.for: Radiator area, cooling mechanism and 250 kW peak solar power capacity.
